newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH C.BANK SELLS DLRS FOR LIRA - BANKERS.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH C.BANK SELLS DLRS FOR LIRA - BANKERS.

text.p: Turkish central bank intervened in late afternoon trade on Friday to halt the fall in the local currency against the dollar, fuelled by political concerns, bankers said.
They said the central bank's dollar sales began at around 134,050 lira and forced banks to lower their dollar bids to 133,850 lira.

The lira had ended at 134,050 against the dollar on Thursday following heavy central bank intervention in the afternoon to curb dollar demand boosted by political fears as well as high currency in circulation and a firm dollar/mark parity.
Political concerns over the fate of Turkey's Islamist-led coalition government mounted on Thursday when markets opened after a 6-1/2 day holiday.
The markets are nervous ahead of Saturday's National Security Council (MGK) meeting.

The coalition's conservative wing DYP is uneasy because of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's failure to implement an anti-Islamist crackdown demanded by the secularist army at a February 28 MGK meeting.
